consensus_summary: Tzitzit are garment tassels or fringes commanded as a visible reminder to remember and obey the LORD’s commandments, thereby expressing covenant holiness and loyalty.
book_summary: Tzitzit are tassels attached to garment corners; seeing them reminds the wearer to remember and perform all the LORD’s commandments.
consensus_core_identification: A divinely commanded garment fringe functioning as a visual reminder to remember and obey God’s commandments.
book_core_identification: A garment-corner tassel functioning as a visual reminder to remember and do all the LORD’s commandments.
boundary_disagreement: None. The consensus adds secondary associations such as holiness and covenant identity, but these elaborate rather than alter the same explicit mnemonic function.
rationale: The book states essentially the same core identification unanimously given by the blind responses and directly expressed in Numbers 15:38–39. Differences are limited to wording and the consensus’s additional theological context; the book neither narrows nor broadens the relevant class of tassels or their primary symbolic function.
strongest_objection: The entry prints only Numbers 15:38–39 rather than verse 40 or Deuteronomy 22:12, so it does not independently support every broader consensus association, especially holiness and covenant identity. Nevertheless, the printed text explicitly and fully supports the book’s own core claim.
